newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Time is money, late HK property agents find out.
newsitem.headline: Time is money, late HK property agents find out.

text.p: Time really is money, Hong Kong property agents found out, when the territory's top appeal court ruled their tardiness cost them a deal on a luxury flat -- and the five-fold appreciation in its value since the sale.

When agents from Union Eagle Ltd showed up 10 minutes late to seal a deal on a HK$4.2 million flat in September 1991, Golden Achievement Ltd rescinded the contract and pocketed the deposit, the South China Morning Post newspaper reported on Wednesday. The Privy Council ended a lengthy legal row over the HK$420,000 deposit and the flat in Tai Tam Road on the south side of Hong Kong island -- now valued at HK$20 million -- by saying a contract is a contract.
"The fact is the purchaser was late. Any suggestion that relief can be obtained on the ground that he was only slightly late is bound to lead to arguments over how late is too late," the court said.
